transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Since we're gearing up for the Saturday evening premiere at the Riverside Courtyard, I'd like to start coordinating our pre-opening routine. Before I can approve the final operating plan and audience admission, I need to check in with production, insurance, and talent coordination. Could each of you bring me up to speed on where things stand on your end?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a serious safety concern. My production safety check this morning found that the courtyard screen rig is rated for sustained wind up to 18 mph, but the Saturday forecast is 22 mph. That exceeds the rig's rating. Harbor Hall, our alternate venue, has a certified indoor rig and a maximum audience capacity of 600. I haven't entered this in the shared production log yet, but given the wind forecast, I don't think we can safely proceed with the courtyard as-is.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important insurance issue. I confirmed with our insurer today that the event policy only covers the screening if the certificate of insurance naming both the festival and Harbor Hall is filed before doors open. The certificate we currently have for the courtyard does not satisfy that endorsement. I have the insurer's written confirmation, but I haven't uploaded it to the venue file yet.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have an important scheduling constraint from talent coordination. I confirmed with the lead guest's agent this afternoon that the guest is available for the question-and-answer session only from 7:45 PM to 8:10 PM, so the session must begin at exactly 7:45 PM. This confirmation is still in my email and hasn't been added to the festival schedule yet, so no one else has seen it until now.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Thank you all for bringing these critical issues forward. Sofia, the lead guest is only available for the Q&A from 7:45 PM to 8:10 PM, so we must start the session at exactly 7:45 PM. Based on these three findings, I'm inclined to move the premiere to Harbor Hall to resolve the safety and insurance issues, set audience admission at 600, ensure the correct certificate is filed before doors, and schedule the Q&A to begin at 7:45 PM. Before I formalize this in the operating plan, does anyone see any problems with this approach or have additional information I should consider?

transcript.text: Mara, from a production standpoint, moving to Harbor Hall resolves the safety concern I flagged — the indoor rig is certified and the 22 mph wind forecast becomes a non-issue.
